help.title: Help & support
help.lead: Answers for the clinic team — from the first booking to month-end payroll.
help.no_results_text: Try another word, or browse the topics.
help.contact_text: Write to us with the clinic name and what you were trying to do — a screenshot helps.
help.contact_none: Ask your clinic owner or manager — they can adjust roles, settings and staff logins.

items.q: What should I set up first?
items.a: Add your doctors with their working hours and consultation fee, then your services and prices. After that, create logins for your staff so each person signs in with their own account.

items.q: How do I switch between Arabic and English?
items.a: Use the language button in the top bar. Your choice is remembered on this device. Doctor names and services can have both an Arabic and an English name.

items.q: Can I use DocBook on my phone?
items.a: Yes. Every screen works in the mobile browser — the bottom bar gives quick access to the calendar, front desk and patients.

items.q: I manage more than one clinic. Do I need another account?
items.a: No. One login can belong to several clinics. Use the clinic switcher in the menu to move between them; each clinic's data stays completely separate.

items.q: How do I book an appointment?
items.a: Open Appointments and choose New appointment. Pick the doctor, service and date — only free times inside the doctor's working hours are offered, so double bookings can't happen.

items.q: How does online booking work?
items.a: When online booking is turned on, patients book from your clinic's public page. Their requests arrive as pending appointments and you get a notification to confirm them.

items.q: A doctor is away for a day. What do I do?
items.a: Add a day off on the doctor's profile. That day disappears from the available times, both for staff and for online booking.

items.q: What is the difference between cancelled and no-show?
items.a: Cancelled means the visit was called off in advance and the time is freed. No-show means the patient did not come; it stays on record for follow-up.

items.q: How does the waiting room work?
items.a: Check patients in when they arrive, call them in when the doctor is ready, and take payment at checkout. The front desk shows who is waiting and for how long.

items.q: How are discounts recorded?
items.a: At checkout enter the amount the patient actually pays and the discount percentage. The invoice keeps both, so reports show the real amount collected.

items.q: An invoice was entered by mistake.
items.a: Someone allowed to manage billing can void the invoice. The visit goes back to unpaid and the change is kept in the audit log.

items.q: Which payment methods are supported?
items.a: Cash, card, bank transfer, insurance and digital wallets. For insurance, choose the insurance company so claims can be followed up.

items.q: How do I set a doctor's working hours?
items.a: Edit the doctor and set the hours for each day, with up to two shifts and a break. The slot length decides how far apart appointment times are.

items.q: Can a doctor have their own login?
items.a: Yes. Create a staff login with the Doctor role and link it to the doctor profile. The doctor then sees only their own schedule and patients.

items.q: Where is the consultation fee used?
items.a: It is the default price of a visit when no service with its own price is chosen. You can hide it from the public booking page.

items.q: How do I add a staff member?
items.a: Go to Staff & permissions, add the person's name and e-mail and pick a role. Each person signs in with their own account and sets their own password — never share one login.

items.q: Can I change what a role can do?
items.a: The clinic owner can adjust permissions or create custom roles. The built-in roles below are a good starting point for most clinics.

items.q: Someone left the clinic.
items.a: Disable their login from Staff & permissions. They are signed out immediately and their past work stays on record.

items.q: Who can read and write clinical notes?
items.a: Doctors write the notes, diagnosis and prescriptions. Nurses record vital signs and can read the record. Reception and accounting staff don't see clinical notes.

items.q: How do I write a visit note?
items.a: Open the visit from My day or the calendar. Record vital signs, then the notes in SOAP format (subjective, objective, assessment, plan) and the diagnosis.

items.q: Can I print a prescription?
items.a: Yes. Prescriptions print on the clinic letterhead with the patient's name, the medicines, dosage, frequency and duration.

items.q: Where do I see a patient's history?
items.a: The patient's page shows all their visits, notes, prescriptions and invoices in one timeline.

items.q: How is a doctor's pay calculated?
items.a: Net pay = base salary + commission + approved bonuses − approved deductions − approved advances. Commission comes from the invoices issued for that doctor during the month.

items.q: What commission types are there?
items.a: A percentage of each invoice, a fixed amount per visit, or a fixed amount per different patient in the month. You can also set a different rate for specific services.

items.q: Why can't I approve my own adjustment?
items.a: Bonuses, deductions and advances need a second person to approve them. This protects the clinic and the doctor; the clinic owner is the only exception.

items.q: What happens when I mark a month as paid?
items.a: The figures of that moment are stored for the payslip and the month is locked. If you need to correct something, undo the payment, fix it and mark it paid again.

items.q: How do I track stock?
items.a: Add each item with its unit and a reorder level. Record restocks as Received, usage as Used, and physical counts as Count — every change is kept in the item's history.

items.q: How do low-stock alerts work?
items.a: When an item reaches its reorder level, people who can see supplies get a notification. If the supplier has an e-mail address, a restock request is e-mailed to them once.

items.q: Who can see what supplies are worth?
items.a: The stock value (stock × unit cost) is shown only to staff who can see the clinic's financial figures.

items.q: Who can see patient data?
items.a: Only staff of your clinic, and only what their role allows. Data from different clinics is always kept apart.

items.q: Is there a record of who changed what?
items.a: Yes. Important actions — edits, deletions, payments, approvals — are written to an audit log that the owner and manager can review.

items.q: I forgot my password.
items.a: Use “Forgot password” on the sign-in page to receive a reset link by e-mail. The link works once and expires after a short time.

items.q: How do I sign out other devices?
items.a: From your account security page you can see active sessions and end the ones you don't recognise.

items.q: Can I export my data?
items.a: Lists such as invoices, expenses, payroll and supplies have an Export button that downloads a CSV or Excel file of the current filters.

items.q: Why don't I see the Export button?
items.a: Exporting needs the data export permission. Ask the clinic owner or manager if your work requires it.

items.q: Who can back up or delete the clinic's data?
items.a: Only the clinic owner. These actions ask you to type the clinic name to confirm.
